sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Notice of Intent to Issue NOFO DE-FOA-0003649: Leveraging Domestic Infrastructure and Resources to Unleash Alternative Chemicals, Fuels and Feedstocks
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Golden Field Office for funding under the 'Notice of Intent to Issue NOFO DE-FOA-0003649: Leveraging Domestic Infrastructure and Resources to Unleash Alternative Chemicals, Fuels and Feedstocks'. Requesting $10,000,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Notice of Intent to Issue NOFO DE-FOA-0003649: Leveraging Domestic Infrastructure and Resources to Unleash Alternative Chemicals, Fuels and Feedstocks', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $10,000,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Mid-scale Research Infrastructure-1
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the U.S. National Science Foundation for funding under the 'Mid-scale Research Infrastructure-1'. Requesting $10,000,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Mid-scale Research Infrastructure-1', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $10,000,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Health and Extreme Weather Research Coordination and Data Center (U2C - Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Health and Extreme Weather Research Coordination and Data Center (U2C - Clinical Trial Not Allowed)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Health and Extreme Weather Research Coordination and Data Center (U2C - Clinical Trial Not Allowed)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Grid Supply Chain Alternatives to Lead Energy Dominance (SCALED)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Energy Technology Laboratory for funding under the 'Grid Supply Chain Alternatives to Lead Energy Dominance (SCALED)'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Grid Supply Chain Alternatives to Lead Energy Dominance (SCALED)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

Requesting $10,000,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Research Infrastructure in the Social and Behavioral Sciences', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $10,000,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

action_steps.title: Designate Lead Author & Division PM
action_steps.action: Appoint principal author, verify SAM.gov active UEI, and initiate Grants.gov Workspace package.

action_steps.title: Secure Matching Funds & NICRA Clearance
action_steps.action: Convene budget review to lock in required 20% non-federal matching commitments and calculate approved indirect rates.

action_steps.title: Draft Technical Narrative & Solicit Partner Letters
action_steps.action: Complete first full draft of 25-page project narrative, collect letters of support, and assemble work plan.

action_steps.title: Internal Legal, SPOC & Executive Review
action_steps.action: Execute Governor's EO 12372 intergovernmental review, legal compliance check, and executive briefing sign-off.

action_steps.title: Final AOR Submission on Grants.gov
action_steps.action: Perform final validation check, submit complete application package on Grants.gov, and archive confirmation receipt.

sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the U.S. Mission to Egypt for funding under the 'U.S. Embassy Cairo Public Diplomacy Section  Annual Program Statement'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'U.S. Embassy Cairo Public Diplomacy Section  Annual Program Statement', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: NIOSH Robotics and Intelligent Mining Technology and Workplace Safety Research (U60)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention - ERA for funding under the 'NIOSH Robotics and Intelligent Mining Technology and Workplace Safety Research (U60)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'NIOSH Robotics and Intelligent Mining Technology and Workplace Safety Research (U60)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:

- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts

Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Environmental Protection Agency for funding under the '2026 Diesel Emissions Reduction Act (DERA) National Program'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the '2026 Diesel Emissions Reduction Act (DERA) National Program', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Limited Competition: Small Grant Program for Mentored Research Career Development Award Recipients (R03) (Clinical Trials Not Allowed)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Limited Competition: Small Grant Program for Mentored Research Career Development Award Recipients (R03) (Clinical Trials Not Allowed)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Limited Competition: Small Grant Program for Mentored Research Career Development Award Recipients (R03) (Clinical Trials Not Allowed)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Federal and State Integration Activities to Advance Cooperation and Regulatory Standards Among Animal Food Safety Regulatory Programs
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Food and Drug Administration for funding under the 'Federal and State Integration Activities to Advance Cooperation and Regulatory Standards Among Animal Food Safety Regulatory Programs'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Federal and State Integration Activities to Advance Cooperation and Regulatory Standards Among Animal Food Safety Regulatory Programs', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Rural Communities Opioid Response Program - Child and Adolescent Behavioral Health
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Health Resources and Services Administration for funding under the 'Rural Communities Opioid Response Program - Child and Adolescent Behavioral Health'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Rural Communities Opioid Response Program - Child and Adolescent Behavioral Health', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Rural Communities Opioid Response Program - Community Systems Development
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Health Resources and Services Administration for funding under the 'Rural Communities Opioid Response Program - Community Systems Development'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Rural Communities Opioid Response Program - Community Systems Development', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).

- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts

Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Affordable Rural Cooperative (ARC) Energy Program
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Rural Utilities Service for funding under the 'Affordable Rural Cooperative (ARC) Energy Program'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Affordable Rural Cooperative (ARC) Energy Program', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: WaterSMART: Desalination Construction Projects
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Bureau of Reclamation for funding under the 'WaterSMART: Desalination Construction Projects'. Requesting $10,000,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'WaterSMART: Desalination Construction Projects', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $10,000,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).

- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts

Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Limited Competition: Superfund Hazardous Substance Research and Training Program (P42 Clinical Trial Optional)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Limited Competition: Superfund Hazardous Substance Research and Training Program (P42 Clinical Trial Optional)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Limited Competition: Superfund Hazardous Substance Research and Training Program (P42 Clinical Trial Optional)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'NRL Long Range Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) for Basic and Applied Research', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the DOC NOAA - ERA Production for funding under the 'SEFSC Bluefin Tuna Research Program'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'SEFSC Bluefin Tuna Research Program', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).

- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Institutional Network Award for Promoting Kidney, Urologic, and Hematologic Research Training (U2C - Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Institutional Network Award for Promoting Kidney, Urologic, and Hematologic Research Training (U2C - Clinical Trial Not Allowed)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Institutional Network Award for Promoting Kidney, Urologic, and Hematologic Research Training (U2C - Clinical Trial Not Allowed)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Dissemination and Implementation Research in Health (R01 Clinical Trial Optional)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

action_steps.title: Designate Lead Author & Division PM
action_steps.action: Appoint principal author, verify SAM.gov active UEI, and initiate Grants.gov Workspace package.

action_steps.title: Secure Matching Funds & NICRA Clearance
action_steps.action: Convene budget review to lock in required 20% non-federal matching commitments and calculate approved indirect rates.

action_steps.title: Draft Technical Narrative & Solicit Partner Letters
action_steps.action: Complete first full draft of 25-page project narrative, collect letters of support, and assemble work plan.

action_steps.title: Internal Legal, SPOC & Executive Review
action_steps.action: Execute Governor's EO 12372 intergovernmental review, legal compliance check, and executive briefing sign-off.

action_steps.action: Perform final validation check, submit complete application package on Grants.gov, and archive confirmation receipt.

sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Dissemination and Implementation Research in Health (R03 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.

Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.

- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Forecast to Publish a Funding Opportunity Announcement for Limited Competition for the Continuation of the National Consortium on Alcohol and Neurodevelopment in Adolescence (NCANDA) Research Project Sites (U01 Clinical Trials Optional)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Forecast to Publish a Funding Opportunity Announcement for Limited Competition for the Continuation of the National Consortium on Alcohol and Neurodevelopment in Adolescence (NCANDA) Research Project Sites (U01 Clinical Trials Optional)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Forecast to Publish a Funding Opportunity Announcement for Limited Competition for the Continuation of the National Consortium on Alcohol and Neurodevelopment in Adolescence (NCANDA) Research Project Sites (U01 Clinical Trials Optional)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Hubs of Interdisciplinary Research and Training in Global Environmental and Occupational Health (GEOHealth)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Hubs of Interdisciplinary Research and Training in Global Environmental and Occupational Health (GEOHealth)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Hubs of Interdisciplinary Research and Training in Global Environmental and Occupational Health (GEOHealth)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Limited Competition: Chronic Kidney Diseases of UnceRtain Etiology (CKDu) in Agricultural Communities (CURE) Research Consortium- Field Epidemiology Sites
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Limited Competition: Chronic Kidney Diseases of UnceRtain Etiology (CKDu) in Agricultural Communities (CURE) Research Consortium- Field Epidemiology Sites'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Limited Competition: Chronic Kidney Diseases of UnceRtain Etiology (CKDu) in Agricultural Communities (CURE) Research Consortium- Field Epidemiology Sites', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Interdisciplinary Research to Understand the Complex Biology of Resilience to Alzheimer’s and Related Dementias Disease Risk
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Interdisciplinary Research to Understand the Complex Biology of Resilience to Alzheimer’s and Related Dementias Disease Risk'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Interdisciplinary Research to Understand the Complex Biology of Resilience to Alzheimer’s and Related Dementias Disease Risk', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Advanced Laboratories for Accelerating the Reach and Impact of Treatments for Youth and Adults with Mental Illness (ALACRITY) Research Centers', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.

sample_draft.methodology:
