sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Innovative Research to Improve Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander (NHPI) Health Outcomes (R34 - Clinical Trial Optional)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Innovative Research to Improve Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander (NHPI) Health Outcomes (R34 - Clinical Trial Optional)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.

Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.

Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.

- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: HEAL Initiative: Pain Management Effectiveness Research Network: Clinical Trial Planning and Implementation Cooperative Agreement (UG3/UH3 Clinical Trial Required)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'HEAL Initiative: Pain Management Effectiveness Research Network: Clinical Trial Planning and Implementation Cooperative Agreement (UG3/UH3 Clinical Trial Required)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'HEAL Initiative: Pain Management Effectiveness Research Network: Clinical Trial Planning and Implementation Cooperative Agreement (UG3/UH3 Clinical Trial Required)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

action_steps.action: Perform final validation check, submit complete application package on Grants.gov, and archive confirmation receipt.

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health (AIM) Technical Assistance Center
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Health Resources and Services Administration for funding under the 'Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health (AIM) Technical Assistance Center'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health (AIM) Technical Assistance Center', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

Without federal support under the 'CAPSTONE Centers for Multidisciplinary Research in Child Abuse and Neglect', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Health Workforce Research Center (HWRC)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Health Resources and Services Administration for funding under the 'Health Workforce Research Center (HWRC)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Health Workforce Research Center (HWRC)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:

- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: ERDC Broad Agency Announcement
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Engineer Research and Development Center for funding under the 'ERDC Broad Agency Announcement'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'ERDC Broad Agency Announcement', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Risk and Protective Factors of Family Health and Family Level Interventions (R01 Clinical Trial Optional)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Risk and Protective Factors of Family Health and Family Level Interventions (R01 Clinical Trial Optional)'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Risk and Protective Factors of Family Health and Family Level Interventions (R01 Clinical Trial Optional)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'CHEERS Open Period 2 - All Technical Areas', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: BJA FY 2026 Missing and Unidentified Human Remains (MUHR) Program
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Bureau of Justice Assistance for funding under the 'BJA FY 2026 Missing and Unidentified Human Remains (MUHR) Program'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'BJA FY 2026 Missing and Unidentified Human Remains (MUHR) Program', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: F26AS00084 Aquatic Invasive Species Grants to Great Lakes Tribes - Fiscal Year 2026 Great Lakes Restoration Initiative
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Fish and Wildlife Service for funding under the 'F26AS00084 Aquatic Invasive Species Grants to Great Lakes Tribes - Fiscal Year 2026 Great Lakes Restoration Initiative'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'F26AS00084 Aquatic Invasive Species Grants to Great Lakes Tribes - Fiscal Year 2026 Great Lakes Restoration Initiative', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Glioblastoma Therapeutics Network (GTN) (U19 Clinical Trial Required)'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Glioblastoma Therapeutics Network (GTN) (U19 Clinical Trial Required)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'BJA FY26 State Criminal Alien Assistance Program (SCAAP)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.

Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Women's Initiative for Screening and Health (WISH)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: FY 2027 – 2029 Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), National Marine Fisheries Service
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the DOC NOAA - ERA Production for funding under the 'FY 2027 – 2029 Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), National Marine Fisheries Service'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'FY 2027 – 2029 Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), National Marine Fisheries Service', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Emergency Competitive Revision to Existing NIH Awards (Emergency Supplement - Clinical Trial Optional)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Emergency Competitive Revision to Existing NIH Awards (Emergency Supplement - Clinical Trial Optional)'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Emergency Competitive Revision to Existing NIH Awards (Emergency Supplement - Clinical Trial Optional)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:

- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts

Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the U.S. National Science Foundation for funding under the 'Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE)'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the DARPA - Information Processing Technologies Office for funding under the 'Information Processing Techniques Office Office-Wide'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Information Processing Techniques Office Office-Wide', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.

sample_draft.methodology:

- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: ROSS Rapid Response Program
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Department of Housing and Urban Development for funding under the 'ROSS Rapid Response Program'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'ROSS Rapid Response Program', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Interventions to expand cancer screening and preventive services to ADVANCE health in populations that experience health disparities (R01, Clinical Trial Required)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Interventions to expand cancer screening and preventive services to ADVANCE health in populations that experience health disparities (R01, Clinical Trial Required)'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Interventions to expand cancer screening and preventive services to ADVANCE health in populations that experience health disparities (R01, Clinical Trial Required)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Pioneering Aerospace Capabilities, Engineering and Research (PACER)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Air Force -- Research Lab for funding under the 'Pioneering Aerospace Capabilities, Engineering and Research (PACER)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Pioneering Aerospace Capabilities, Engineering and Research (PACER)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Growing Research Access for Nationally Transformative Economic Development (GRANTED)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the U.S. National Science Foundation for funding under the 'Growing Research Access for Nationally Transformative Economic Development (GRANTED)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Growing Research Access for Nationally Transformative Economic Development (GRANTED)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'NIAID Resource-Related Research Projects (R24 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)'. Requesting $2,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'NIAID Resource-Related Research Projects (R24 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $2,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Pediatric and Reproductive Environmental Health Scholars (PREHS) Program', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.

Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.

- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: MISSION ITALY ANNUAL PROGRAM STATEMENT 2023
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the U.S. Mission to Italy for funding under the 'MISSION ITALY ANNUAL PROGRAM STATEMENT 2023'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'MISSION ITALY ANNUAL PROGRAM STATEMENT 2023', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Bridge2AI Network for AI Health Science
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the National Institutes of Health for funding under the 'Bridge2AI Network for AI Health Science'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Bridge2AI Network for AI Health Science', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: First Responders-Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Act
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Adminis for funding under the 'First Responders-Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Act'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'First Responders-Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Act', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings

sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Administration for Children and Families for funding under the 'Tribal Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program: Development and Implementation Grants'. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Tribal Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program: Development and Implementation Grants', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.

Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:

Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.

- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award

sample_draft.title: North Carolina Strategic Implementation Project: Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program (MIECHV)
sample_draft.abstract: The North Carolina Department of Transportation respectfully submits this application to the Health Resources and Services Administration for funding under the 'Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program (MIECHV)'. Requesting $1,500,000 in federal assistance, this initiative will strategically advance North Carolina's infrastructure, public service delivery, and community resilience. Targeting high-need communities and leveraging robust state and local partnerships, the project ensures rapid operational rollout, rigorous performance monitoring, and sustained long-term public benefit.
sample_draft.statement_of_need: North Carolina continues to experience rapid population growth, climate impacts, and economic transition that place unprecedented pressure on local infrastructure and regional service capacity. Communities across the state—ranging from Tier 1 distressed rural counties to expanding metropolitan corridors—require targeted investment to maintain environmental health, public safety, and modern infrastructure. Without federal support under the 'Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program (MIECHV)', these urgent needs will outpace state and municipal capital budgets. This proposal establishes a timely, data-driven intervention aligned directly with published state strategic priorities.
smart_objectives: Objective 1 (Months 1-6): Complete comprehensive engineering scoping, stakeholder coordination, and environmental clearances.
Objective 2 (Months 7-18): Deploy initial project phases, achieving 50% capital installation and community outreach milestones.
Objective 3 (Months 19-30): Fully operationalize project infrastructure, serving over 150,000 North Carolina residents.
Objective 4 (Months 31-36): Conduct rigorous post-implementation audit, verify KPI targets, and transition to permanent state operation.
sample_draft.methodology:
Phase I (Design & Alignment): Inter-agency kickoff, finalize procurement specifications, and execute sub-recipient MOUs.
Phase II (Implementation & Deployment): Vendor selection under state procurement standards, phased construction/rollout, and bi-weekly milestone reviews.
Phase III (Performance Audit & Closeout): Independent evaluation, compliance verification, and delivery of final data reports to federal grantor.
sample_draft.budget_narrative:
Total Project Budget: $1,500,000 (Federal Share: 80% / State-Local Match: 20%).
- Personnel & Fringe: 32% (Project Director, Senior Engineers, and Compliance Specialist)
- Contractual & Equipment: 52% (Infrastructure vendors, hardware procurement, and technical contractors)
- Travel & Direct Operational Costs: 4% (On-site inspections and stakeholder convenings)
- Indirect Costs (NICRA): 12% (Cognizant state agency negotiated rate for administration and oversight)
kpis: 100% adherence to project milestone timeline within 36 months of award
Direct service delivery to at least 25 North Carolina municipalities or regional districts
Demonstrated 30% increase in operational capacity or risk reduction metrics
Clean single-audit compliance and zero unallowable cost findings
